474:     /// <summary>
475:     /// Figures out which Steam Workshop id a local mod folder corresponds to.
476:     /// Tries the "<id> <name>" naming convention this app installs mods
477:     /// under first, then falls back to scanning any mod.info file inside for
478:     /// a purely-numeric id= line (some mods happen to use one).
479:     /// </summary>
480:     private static bool TryExtractWorkshopId(string folderPath, out string id)
481:     {
482:         id = "";
483:         var name = Path.GetFileName(folderPath);
484:         if (name.StartsWith("_")) return false; // skip internal folders like _backups
485: 
486:         var m = Regex.Match(name, @"^(\d+)");
487:         if (m.Success)
488:         {
489:             id = m.Groups[1].Value;
490:             return true;
491:         }
492: 
493:         try
494:         {
495:             foreach (var infoFile in Directory.EnumerateFiles(folderPath, "mod.info", SearchOption.AllDirectories))
496:             {
497:                 foreach (var line in File.ReadAllLines(infoFile))
498:                 {
499:                     var lm = Regex.Match(line.Trim(), @"^id\s*=\s*(\d+)\s*$", RegexOptions.IgnoreCase);
500:                     if (lm.Success)
501:                     {
502:                         id = lm.Groups[1].Value;
503:                         return true;
504:                     }
505:                 }
506:             }
507:         }
508:         catch
509:         {
510:             // Unreadable folder -- treat as unresolvable.
511:         }
512: 
513:         return false;
514:     }

516:     /// <summary>
517:     /// Normalizes a mod identifier for dependency matching: lowercase, remove
518:     /// spaces and punctuation, so "NeatUI_Framework" == "neatui framework" ==
519:     /// "NeatUI Framework" when comparing require= values against installed
520:     /// mods' id=/name= fields.
521:     /// </summary>
522:     private static string NormalizeModIdentifier(string value)
523:     {
524:         var sb = new System.Text.StringBuilder(value.Length);
525:         foreach (var c in value)
526:         {
527:             if (char.IsLetterOrDigit(c)) sb.Append(char.ToLowerInvariant(c));
528:         }
529:         return sb.ToString();
530:     }

615:     /// <summary>
616:     /// Scans the mods folder, pulls live details from Steam for each mod,
617:     /// and determines which ones need an update -- this single pass now
618:     /// covers both "list what's installed" and "check for updates" (the
619:     /// tabs used to be separate; merged so there's one source of truth).
620:     /// </summary>
621:     private async Task RefreshDownloadedModsAsync()
622:     {
623:         if (string.IsNullOrWhiteSpace(_settings.ModsFolder) || !Directory.Exists(_settings.ModsFolder))
624:             return;
625: 
626:         AppendLog("Refreshing mod list and checking for updates...");
627:         var records = new List<ModRecord>();
628:         int updatesAvailable = 0;
629: 
630:         // Build an index of every installed mod's declared identifiers (id=/name=
631:         // from its mod.info) -> real workshop id (the numeric folder prefix), plus
632:         // the set of installed workshop ids. This lets require= entries (numeric
633:         // ids or internal names like "\NeatUI_Framework") be resolved purely
634:         // against what is already on disk -- no extra Steam API calls.
635:         var installedWorkshopIds = new HashSet<string>(StringComparer.Ordinal);
636:         var identifierIndex = new Dictionary<string, string>(StringComparer.OrdinalIgnoreCase);
637:         foreach (var dir in Directory.GetDirectories(_settings.ModsFolder))
638:         {
639:             if (!TryExtractWorkshopId(dir, out var knownId)) continue;
640:             installedWorkshopIds.Add(knownId);
641:             foreach (var ident in SteamCmdService.GetModIdentifiers(dir))
642:             {
643:                 var key = NormalizeModIdentifier(ident);
644:                 if (key.Length > 0) identifierIndex.TryAdd(key, knownId);
645:             }
646:         }
647: 
648:         foreach (var dir in Directory.GetDirectories(_settings.ModsFolder))
649:         {
650:             if (!TryExtractWorkshopId(dir, out var id)) continue;
651:             var folderName = Path.GetFileName(dir);
652: 
653:             // Resolve require= entries against the installed-mod index above.
654:             var requires = SteamCmdService.GetRequiresFields(dir);
655:             var missingDeps = new List<string>();
656:             foreach (var req in requires)
657:             {
658:                 bool met = long.TryParse(req, out _)
659:                     ? installedWorkshopIds.Contains(req)
660:                     : identifierIndex.TryGetValue(NormalizeModIdentifier(req), out _);
661:                 if (!met) missingDeps.Add(req);
662:             }
663: 
664:             string title = folderName, posted = "", updated = "", steamVer = "Unknown", creator = "";
665:             bool resolvedRemote = false;
666:             try
667:             {
668:                 var details = await WorkshopApiService.GetDetailsAsync(id);
669:                 title = details.Title;
670:                 posted = details.TimeCreated == default ? "" : details.TimeCreated.ToLocalTime().ToString("dd-MMM-yy h:mm:ss tt");
671:                 updated = details.TimeUpdated == default ? "" : details.TimeUpdated.ToLocalTime().ToString("dd-MMM-yy h:mm:ss tt");
672:                 steamVer = string.IsNullOrEmpty(details.ContentManifestId) ? "Unknown" : details.ContentManifestId;
673:                 resolvedRemote = !string.IsNullOrEmpty(details.ContentManifestId);
674:                 creator = details.Creator;
675:             }
676:             catch
677:             {
678:                 // Offline, or the item was removed -- still show the folder by id.
679:             }
680: 
681:             var hasLocalVersion = _settings.LocalModVersions.TryGetValue(id, out var lv) && !string.IsNullOrEmpty(lv);
682:             var localVer = hasLocalVersion ? lv! : "Unknown";
683:             var installDate = _settings.InstallDates.TryGetValue(id, out var idate) ? idate : "";
684: 
685:             bool needsUpdate;
686:             if (!resolvedRemote)
687:                 needsUpdate = false; // couldn't reach Steam -- don't false-flag
688:             else if (!hasLocalVersion)
689:                 needsUpdate = true; // never tracked (e.g. placed manually) -- flag so the user can decide
690:             else
691:                 needsUpdate = !string.Equals(lv, steamVer, StringComparison.Ordinal);
692: 
693:             if (needsUpdate) updatesAvailable++;
694: 
695:             records.Add(new ModRecord
696:             {
697:                 Folder = folderName,
698:                 FullPath = dir,
699:                 Id = id,
700:                 ModName = title,
701:                 Size = FormatSize(GetDirectorySize(dir)),
702:                 Posted = posted,
703:                 Updated = updated,
704:                 LocalVersion = localVer,
705:                 SteamVersion = steamVer,
706:                 InstallDate = installDate,
707:                 NeedsUpdate = needsUpdate,
708:                 StatusLabel = needsUpdate ? "Update Available" : "Updated",
709:                 Creator = creator,
710:                 Dependencies = requires,
711:                 MissingDependencies = missingDeps,
712:                 MissingDepsCount = missingDeps.Count,
713:             });
714:         }
715: 
716:         _downloadedMods.Clear();
717:         foreach (var r in records) _downloadedMods.Add(r);
718: 
719:         UpdatesAvailableText.Text = $"Mods with updates available: {updatesAvailable}";
720:         UpdateAllButton.IsEnabled = updatesAvailable > 0;
721:         AppendLog($"Refresh complete: {records.Count} mod(s) installed, {updatesAvailable} update(s) available.");
722: 
723:         // Batch 4: kick off the preview/tag/thumbnail fetch for installed mods
724:         // in the background. Tag sidebar + thumbnails fill in as it completes.
725:         _ = LoadInstalledVisualsAsync();
726:     }

730:     /// <summary>
731:     /// Fetches preview_url + tags for the installed mods in one batched API
732:     /// call, downloads any missing thumbnails into the cache (throttled), then
733:     /// rebuilds the tag sidebar. Runs in the background; grids/tiles update in
734:     /// place because ThumbnailPath raises PropertyChanged.
735:     /// </summary>
736:     private async Task LoadInstalledVisualsAsync()
737:     {
738:         try
739:         {
740:             var mods = _downloadedMods.ToList();
741:             if (mods.Count == 0) { RebuildTagSidebar(); return; }
742: 
743:             var visuals = await WorkshopVisualService.GetVisualsAsync(mods.Select(m => m.Id));
744: 
745:             await Task.WhenAll(mods.Select(async m =>
746:             {
747:                 if (!visuals.TryGetValue(m.Id, out var v)) return;
748:                 m.Tags = v.Tags;
749:                 await ThumbnailGate.WaitAsync();
750:                 try
751:                 {
752:                     m.ThumbnailPath = await ThumbnailStore.GetOrDownloadAsync(m.Id, v.PreviewUrl);
753:                 }
754:                 finally
755:                 {
756:                     ThumbnailGate.Release();
757:                 }
758:             }));
759: 
760:             await Dispatcher.InvokeAsync(RebuildTagSidebar);
761:             AppendLog($"Loaded previews/tags for {mods.Count} installed mod(s).");
762:         }
763:         catch (Exception ex)
764:         {
765:             AppendLog($"Could not load mod visuals: {ex.Message}", "WARNING");
766:         }
767:     }

1021:     /// <summary>
1022:     /// Deletes the folder currently on disk for a mod before an update
1023:     /// redownloads it. This matters because SteamCMD's fresh download can
1024:     /// name the mod's folder slightly differently than what's already
1025:     /// installed (renamed subfolder, capitalization change, etc.) -- the
1026:     /// installer only overwrites a folder when the name matches exactly,
1027:     /// so without this step a mismatch leaves the old copy behind and
1028:     /// creates a duplicate instead of replacing it.
1029:     /// </summary>
1030:     private void RemoveOldModFolder(string folderName)
1031:     {
1032:         try
1033:         {
1034:             var path = Path.Combine(_settings.ModsFolder, folderName);
1035:             if (Directory.Exists(path)) Directory.Delete(path, recursive: true);
1036:         }
1037:         catch (Exception ex)
1038:         {
1039:             // Best-effort -- if this fails, the download will still overwrite
1040:             // any folder whose name happens to match exactly.
1041:             AppendLog($"Could not remove old folder \"{folderName}\" before redownload: {ex.Message}", "WARNING");
1042:         }
1043:     }
1044: 
1045:     private void BackupMod(string folderName)
1046:     {
1047:         try
1048:         {
1049:             var src = Path.Combine(_settings.ModsFolder, folderName);
1050:             if (!Directory.Exists(src)) return;
1051:             var backupDir = Path.Combine(_settings.ModsFolder, "_backups", folderName, DateTime.Now.ToString("yyyyMMdd_HHmmss"));
1052:             Directory.CreateDirectory(Path.GetDirectoryName(backupDir)!);
1053:             CopyDirectory(src, backupDir);
1054:         }
1055:         catch
1056:         {
1057:             // Best-effort backup; don't block the update if it fails.
1058:         }
1059:     }
1060: 
1061:     private static void CopyDirectory(string sourceDir, string destDir)
1062:     {
1063:         Directory.CreateDirectory(destDir);
1064:         foreach (var file in Directory.GetFiles(sourceDir))
1065:             File.Copy(file, Path.Combine(destDir, Path.GetFileName(file)), overwrite: true);
1066:         foreach (var dir in Directory.GetDirectories(sourceDir))
1067:             CopyDirectory(dir, Path.Combine(destDir, Path.GetFileName(dir)));
1068:     }

1103:     /// "Show Deps" button on an Installed Mods row. The Steam Workshop page for
1104:     /// the selected mod is the authoritative source of its dependencies: the
1105:     /// "Required items" section lists every dependency (workshop id + name),
1106:     /// whether or not it's installed. So the popup is populated from that page
1107:     /// and each entry is annotated installed/missing by comparing its workshop id
1108:     /// against the installed-mod index.

1110:     /// This lookup happens ONLY here, on explicit user action -- never during
1111:     /// startup or the Installed Mods refresh -- and fetches ONLY this mod's page
1112:     /// (no recursive dependency-page requests). Results are cached per session
1113:     /// and concurrent duplicate clicks are ignored.

98:     /// "collection" style items do), so this can install more than one
99:     /// destination folder per item. Returns every folder that was created.
100:     /// </summary>
101:     public static async Task<List<string>> DownloadModAsync(string workshopId, string destFolder, Action<string> log)
102:     {
103:         // Serialize downloads -- SteamCMD does not support concurrent instances well.
104:         await RunLock.WaitAsync();
105:         try
106:         {
107:             await EnsureSteamCmdAsync(log);
108:             await BootstrapAsync(log);
109: 
110:             log($"Downloading workshop item {workshopId} via SteamCMD...");
111:             var args = new[]
112:             {
113:                 "+force_install_dir", SteamCmdDir,
114:                 "+login", "anonymous",
115:                 "+workshop_download_item", AppId, workshopId,
116:                 "+quit",
117:             };
118:             int exitCode = await RunSteamCmdAsync(args, log);
119: 
120:             var downloadedPath = GetContentPath(workshopId);
121:             bool hasFiles = Directory.Exists(downloadedPath) &&
122:                             Directory.EnumerateFileSystemEntries(downloadedPath).Any();
123: 
124:             if (!hasFiles)
125:             {
126:                 throw new Exception(
127:                     $"SteamCMD did not produce any files for item {workshopId} " +
128:                     $"(exit code {exitCode}). The item may be invalid, removed, or restricted.");
129:             }
130: 
131:             if (exitCode != 0)
132:             {
133:                 // SteamCMD sometimes self-updates again right after a
134:                 // successful download and returns a nonzero code from that
135:                 // unrelated relaunch. Since the files are present, treat
136:                 // this as benign.
137:                 log($"Note: SteamCMD returned exit code {exitCode}, but the mod files " +
138:                     $"were found on disk — continuing.");
139:             }
140: 
141:             var installedPaths = new List<string>();
142:             var modsSubdir = Path.Combine(downloadedPath, "mods");
143: 
144:             if (Directory.Exists(modsSubdir) && Directory.GetDirectories(modsSubdir).Length > 0)
145:             {
146:                 // Normal case: PZ workshop items ship their actual mod
147:                 // folder(s) under a "mods" subfolder.
148:                 foreach (var modDir in Directory.GetDirectories(modsSubdir))
149:                 {
150:                     var rawFolderName = Path.GetFileName(modDir);
151:                     // Prefer mod.info's "name=" (the human-readable display
152:                     // name) over the raw subfolder name -- mod authors very
153:                     // commonly name that physical folder after their internal
154:                     // "id=" instead, which produces cryptic, non-descriptive
155:                     // installed folder names otherwise.
156:                     var modFolderName = GetModDisplayName(modDir) ?? rawFolderName;
157:                     var dest = Path.Combine(destFolder, $"{workshopId} {modFolderName}");
158:                     if (Directory.Exists(dest)) Directory.Delete(dest, recursive: true);
159:                     CopyDirectory(modDir, dest);
160:                     installedPaths.Add(dest);
161:                     log($"Installed mod to {dest}");
162:                 }
163:             }
164:             else
165:             {
166:                 // Fallback for oddly-structured items with no "mods" folder --
167:                 // install the whole downloaded item as-is.
168:                 var dest = Path.Combine(destFolder, workshopId);
169:                 if (Directory.Exists(dest)) Directory.Delete(dest, recursive: true);
170:                 CopyDirectory(downloadedPath, dest);
171:                 installedPaths.Add(dest);
172:                 log($"Note: no 'mods' subfolder found in this item; installed raw content to {dest}");
173:             }
174: 
175:             return installedPaths;
176:         }
177:         finally
178:         {
179:             RunLock.Release();
180:         }
181:     }

183:     /// <summary>
184:     /// Reads mod.info inside a mod folder and returns its "name=" value
185:     /// (sanitized for use as a filesystem folder name), or null if there's
186:     /// no mod.info or no name field.
187:     /// </summary>
188:     private static string? GetModDisplayName(string modDir)
189:     {
190:         try
191:         {
192:             var infoPath = Path.Combine(modDir, "mod.info");
193:             if (!File.Exists(infoPath)) return null;
194: 
195:             foreach (var line in File.ReadAllLines(infoPath))
196:             {
197:                 var m = Regex.Match(line.Trim(), @"^name\s*=\s*(.+)$", RegexOptions.IgnoreCase);
198:                 if (m.Success)
199:                 {
200:                     var name = m.Groups[1].Value.Trim();
201:                     if (!string.IsNullOrWhiteSpace(name))
202:                         return SanitizeFileName(name);
203:                 }
204:             }
205:         }
206:         catch
207:         {
208:             // Unreadable mod.info -- fall back to the raw folder name.
209:         }
210:         return null;
211:     }
212: 
213:     /// <summary>
214:     /// Reads mod.info inside a mod folder and returns every value declared in
215:     /// its require= entries. Values are either a numeric workshop id or an
216:     /// internal mod identifier (often backslash-prefixed, e.g. "\NeatUI_Framework");
217:     /// the backslash prefix and any comma/semicolon separation are stripped.
218:     /// Returns an empty list when there is no readable mod.info / no require field.
219:     /// </summary>
220:     public static List<string> GetRequiresFields(string modDir)
221:     {
222:         var requires = new List<string>();
223:         try
224:         {
225:             var infoPath = Path.Combine(modDir, "mod.info");
226:             if (!File.Exists(infoPath)) return requires;
227: 
228:             foreach (var line in File.ReadAllLines(infoPath))
229:             {
230:                 var m = Regex.Match(line.Trim(), @"^require\s*=\s*(.+)$", RegexOptions.IgnoreCase);
231:                 if (!m.Success) continue;
232: 
233:                 var value = m.Groups[1].Value.Trim();
234:                 if (string.IsNullOrWhiteSpace(value)) continue;
235: 
236:                 foreach (var part in value.Split(new[] { ',', ';' }, StringSplitOptions.RemoveEmptyEntries))
237:                 {
238:                     var id = part.Trim();
239:                     if (id.StartsWith("\\")) id = id[1..].Trim();
240:                     if (id.Length > 0) requires.Add(id);
241:                 }
242:             }
243:         }
244:         catch
245:         {
246:             // Unreadable mod.info -- no dependencies can be declared.
247:         }
248:         return requires;
249:     }
250: 
251:     /// <summary>
252:     /// Reads mod.info inside a mod folder and returns its declared identifier
253:     /// values (the letter-based "id=" and the human-readable "name="). These are
254:     /// used ONLY to resolve a require= reference (e.g. "\NeatUI_Framework") to the
255:     /// real workshop id of an installed mod -- never to identify a mod on its own.
256:     /// </summary>
257:     public static List<string> GetModIdentifiers(string modDir)
258:     {
259:         var ids = new List<string>();
260:         try
261:         {
262:             var infoPath = Path.Combine(modDir, "mod.info");
263:             if (!File.Exists(infoPath)) return ids;
264: 
265:             foreach (var line in File.ReadAllLines(infoPath))
266:             {
267:                 var m = Regex.Match(line.Trim(), @"^(id|name)\s*=\s*(.+)$", RegexOptions.IgnoreCase);
268:                 if (m.Success && !string.IsNullOrWhiteSpace(m.Groups[2].Value))
269:                     ids.Add(m.Groups[2].Value.Trim());
270:             }
271:         }
272:         catch
273:         {
274:             // Unreadable mod.info -- no identifiers to match against.
275:         }
276:         return ids;
277:     }
278: 
279:     private static string SanitizeFileName(string name)
280:     {
281:         foreach (var c in Path.GetInvalidFileNameChars())
282:             name = name.Replace(c, '_');
283:         return name;
284:     }
285: 
286:     private static void CopyDirectory(string sourceDir, string destDir)
287:     {
288:         Directory.CreateDirectory(destDir);
289:         foreach (var file in Directory.GetFiles(sourceDir))
290:             File.Copy(file, Path.Combine(destDir, Path.GetFileName(file)), overwrite: true);
291:         foreach (var dir in Directory.GetDirectories(sourceDir))
292:             CopyDirectory(dir, Path.Combine(destDir, Path.GetFileName(dir)));
293:     }
294: }

13: /// WorkshopApiService is intentionally untouched (it stays minimal), so this
14: /// service exists to grab the extra fields (preview_url / tags) the app now

16: /// (up to 100 ids per call) so one request covers all installed mods.
17: /// </summary>
18: public class WorkshopVisual
19: {
20:     public string Id { get; set; } = "";
21:     public string PreviewUrl { get; set; } = "";
22:     public List<string> Tags { get; set; } = new();
23: }

26: {
27:     private const string Endpoint =
28:         "https://api.steampowered.com/ISteamRemoteStorage/GetPublishedFileDetails/v1/";
29: 
30:     private const int MaxPerRequest = 100;
31: 
32:     private static readonly HttpClient Http = new();
33: 
34:     /// <summary>
35:     /// Fetches preview_url + tags for the given workshop ids in as few API
36:     /// calls as possible. Never throws for an individual item; a hard network
37:     /// failure throws and is caught by the caller.
38:     /// </summary>
39:     public static async Task<Dictionary<string, WorkshopVisual>> GetVisualsAsync(IEnumerable<string> ids)
40:     {
41:         var idList = ids.Where(id => !string.IsNullOrEmpty(id)).Distinct().ToList();
42:         var result = new Dictionary<string, WorkshopVisual>(StringComparer.Ordinal);
43: 
44:         foreach (var chunk in Chunks(idList, MaxPerRequest))
45:         {
46:             var content = new Dictionary<string, string> { ["itemcount"] = chunk.Count.ToString() };
47:             for (int i = 0; i < chunk.Count; i++)
48:                 content[$"publishedfileids[{i}]"] = chunk[i];
49: 
50:             var resp = await Http.PostAsync(Endpoint, new FormUrlEncodedContent(content));
51:             resp.EnsureSuccessStatusCode();
52: 
53:             using var doc = JsonDocument.Parse(await resp.Content.ReadAsStringAsync());
54:             var list = doc.RootElement.GetProperty("response").GetProperty("publishedfiledetails");
55: 
56:             foreach (var el in list.EnumerateArray())
57:             {
58:                 var id = GetString(el, "publishedfileid");
59:                 if (id == null) continue;
60: 
61:                 var visual = new WorkshopVisual
62:                 {
63:                     Id = id,
64:                     PreviewUrl = GetString(el, "preview_url") ?? "",
65:                 };

<Window x:Class="PZWorkshopDownloader.MainWindow"
        xmlns="http://schemas.microsoft.com/winfx/2006/xaml/presentation"
        xmlns:x="http://schemas.microsoft.com/winfx/2006/xaml"
        xmlns:wv2="clr-namespace:Microsoft.Web.WebView2.Wpf;assembly=Microsoft.Web.WebView2.Wpf"
        Title="Project Zomboid Workshop Downloader"
        Height="880" Width="1300" MinHeight="600" MinWidth="900"
        FontSize="{DynamicResource UIFontSizeGeneral}"
        Background="{DynamicResource BgDark}">

    <Window.Resources>

        <!-- Batch 4: shared tile thumbnail block (initial-letter placeholder until
             ThumbnailPath arrives; the image then covers it). Width/Height follow
             the app-wide ModTileSize resource so the slider resizes every tile. -->
        <DataTemplate x:Key="TileThumbnail">
            <Grid Width="{DynamicResource ModTileSize}" Height="{DynamicResource ModTileSize}">
                <Border Background="{DynamicResource BgField}" CornerRadius="6"
                        BorderBrush="{DynamicResource BorderCol}" BorderThickness="1">
                    <TextBlock Text="{Binding Initial}" FontSize="26" FontWeight="Bold"
                               Foreground="{DynamicResource FgText}" Opacity="0.45"
                               HorizontalAlignment="Center" VerticalAlignment="Center"/>
                </Border>
                <Image Source="{Binding ThumbnailPath}" Stretch="UniformToFill" Margin="2.5">
                    <Image.Style>
                        <Style TargetType="Image">
                            <Setter Property="Visibility" Value="Visible"/>
                            <Style.Triggers>
                                <DataTrigger Binding="{Binding ThumbnailPath}" Value="">
                                    <Setter Property="Visibility" Value="Collapsed"/>
                                </DataTrigger>
                            </Style.Triggers>
                        </Style>
                    </Image.Style>
                </Image>
            </Grid>
        </DataTemplate>

        <ContextMenu x:Key="DownloadsRowContextMenu">
            <MenuItem Header="Remove From List" Click="RemoveDownloadEntry_Click"
                      Tag="{Binding PlacementTarget.Tag, RelativeSource={RelativeSource AncestorType=ContextMenu}}"/>
        </ContextMenu>

        <ContextMenu x:Key="InstalledModsRowContextMenu">
            <MenuItem Header="Open Mod Folder" Click="OpenFolder_Click"
                      Tag="{Binding PlacementTarget.Tag.FullPath, RelativeSource={RelativeSource AncestorType=ContextMenu}}"/>
            <MenuItem Header="Open Mod Page" Click="ModPage_Click"
                      Tag="{Binding PlacementTarget.Tag.Id, RelativeSource={RelativeSource AncestorType=ContextMenu}}"/>
            <Separator/>
            <MenuItem Header="Update This Mod" Click="UpdateSingleMod_Click"
                      IsEnabled="{Binding PlacementTarget.Tag.NeedsUpdate, RelativeSource={RelativeSource AncestorType=ContextMenu}}"
                      Tag="{Binding PlacementTarget.Tag, RelativeSource={RelativeSource AncestorType=ContextMenu}}"/>
            <MenuItem Header="Force Redownload" Click="ForceRedownloadMod_Click"
                      Tag="{Binding PlacementTarget.Tag, RelativeSource={RelativeSource AncestorType=ContextMenu}}"/>
            <MenuItem Header="Show Dependencies" Click="ShowDeps_Click"
                      IsEnabled="{Binding PlacementTarget.Tag.HasDependencies, RelativeSource={RelativeSource AncestorType=ContextMenu}}"
                      Tag="{Binding PlacementTarget.Tag, RelativeSource={RelativeSource AncestorType=ContextMenu}}"/>
            <Separator/>
            <MenuItem Header="Uninstall" Click="UninstallMod_Click"
                      Tag="{Binding PlacementTarget.Tag, RelativeSource={RelativeSource AncestorType=ContextMenu}}"/>
        </ContextMenu>

        <ContextMenu x:Key="UninstalledModsRowContextMenu">
            <MenuItem Header="Reinstall" Click="ReinstallMod_Click"
                      Tag="{Binding PlacementTarget.Tag, RelativeSource={RelativeSource AncestorType=ContextMenu}}"/>
            <MenuItem Header="Open Mod Page" Click="ModPage_Click"
                      Tag="{Binding PlacementTarget.Tag.Id, RelativeSource={RelativeSource AncestorType=ContextMenu}}"/>
            <Separator/>
            <MenuItem Header="Forget" Click="ForgetUninstalledMod_Click"
                      Tag="{Binding PlacementTarget.Tag, RelativeSource={RelativeSource AncestorType=ContextMenu}}"/>
        </ContextMenu>

        <!-- ============ Tile mode (Batch 4) ============
             Shared styles so all three tile grids stay consistent.
             NOTE: we pulse via Opacity (DoubleAnimation), never by animating a
             brush Color. WPF freezes SolidColorBrush instances inside shared
             DataTemplates, so ColorAnimation on (Foreground).(SolidColorBrush.Color)
             throws "Cannot animate on an immutable object instance". -->

        <!-- Common chrome for every tile button. -->
        <Style x:Key="TileButtonStyle" TargetType="Button">
            <Setter Property="Background" Value="{DynamicResource BgPanel}"/>
            <Setter Property="BorderBrush" Value="{DynamicResource BorderCol}"/>
            <Setter Property="BorderThickness" Value="1"/>
            <Setter Property="Margin" Value="0,0,10,10"/>
            <Setter Property="Padding" Value="6"/>
            <Setter Property="HorizontalContentAlignment" Value="Center"/>
            <Setter Property="Width" Value="{DynamicResource ModTileSize}"/>
        </Style>

        <!-- Mod name text (Installed tiles turn orange+bold when an update is out). -->
        <Style x:Key="TileNameTextStyle" TargetType="TextBlock">
            <Setter Property="TextWrapping" Value="Wrap"/>
            <Setter Property="TextAlignment" Value="Center"/>
            <Setter Property="MaxHeight" Value="34"/>
            <Setter Property="Margin" Value="0,4,0,2"/>
            <Setter Property="FontSize" Value="{DynamicResource UIFontSizeGeneral}"/>
            <Setter Property="Foreground" Value="{DynamicResource FgText}"/>
            <Style.Triggers>
                <DataTrigger Binding="{Binding NeedsUpdate}" Value="True">
                    <Setter Property="Foreground" Value="#FF8C00"/>
                    <Setter Property="FontWeight" Value="Bold"/>
                </DataTrigger>
            </Style.Triggers>
        </Style>

        <!-- Status line shared appearance. -->
        <Style x:Key="TileStatusTextBase" TargetType="TextBlock">
            <Setter Property="FontSize" Value="11"/>
            <Setter Property="HorizontalAlignment" Value="Center"/>
            <Setter Property="FontWeight" Value="Bold"/>
            <Setter Property="Foreground" Value="#3EB489"/>
        </Style>

        <!-- Update status: solid green, orange + opacity pulse when NeedsUpdate. -->
        <Style x:Key="TileUpdateStatusText" TargetType="TextBlock" BasedOn="{StaticResource TileStatusTextBase}">
            <Style.Triggers>
                <DataTrigger Binding="{Binding NeedsUpdate}" Value="True">
                    <Setter Property="Foreground" Value="#FF8C00"/>
                    <DataTrigger.EnterActions>
                        <BeginStoryboard x:Name="TileUpdatePulse">
                            <Storyboard>
                                <DoubleAnimation Storyboard.TargetProperty="Opacity"
                                                 From="1.0" To="0.45"
                                                 Duration="0:0:0.9" AutoReverse="True" RepeatBehavior="Forever"/>
                            </Storyboard>
                        </BeginStoryboard>
                    </DataTrigger.EnterActions>
                    <DataTrigger.ExitActions>
                        <StopStoryboard BeginStoryboardName="TileUpdatePulse"/>
                    </DataTrigger.ExitActions>
                </DataTrigger>
            </Style.Triggers>
        </Style>

        <!-- Requirement status: solid green, orange + opacity pulse when HasMissingDeps. -->
        <Style x:Key="TileRequirementStatusText" TargetType="TextBlock" BasedOn="{StaticResource TileStatusTextBase}">
            <Style.Triggers>
                <DataTrigger Binding="{Binding HasMissingDeps}" Value="True">
                    <Setter Property="Foreground" Value="#FF8C00"/>
                    <DataTrigger.EnterActions>
                        <BeginStoryboard x:Name="TileRequirementPulse">
                            <Storyboard>
                                <DoubleAnimation Storyboard.TargetProperty="Opacity"
                                                 From="1.0" To="0.45"
                                                 Duration="0:0:0.9" AutoReverse="True" RepeatBehavior="Forever"/>
                            </Storyboard>
                        </BeginStoryboard>
                    </DataTrigger.EnterActions>
                    <DataTrigger.ExitActions>
                        <StopStoryboard BeginStoryboardName="TileRequirementPulse"/>
                    </DataTrigger.ExitActions>
                </DataTrigger>
            </Style.Triggers>
        </Style>

    </Window.Resources>

    <Grid Background="{DynamicResource BgDark}">
        <Grid.RowDefinitions>
            <RowDefinition Height="*"/>
            <RowDefinition Height="Auto"/>
        </Grid.RowDefinitions>
        <Grid.ColumnDefinitions>
            <ColumnDefinition Width="*"/>
            <ColumnDefinition x:Name="QueueColumn" Width="0"/>
        </Grid.ColumnDefinitions>

        <TabControl x:Name="MainTabs" Grid.Row="0" Grid.Column="0" Background="{DynamicResource BgPanel}"
                    BorderThickness="0" Margin="0">

            <!-- ============ BROWSER TAB ============ -->
            <TabItem Header="Browser" x:Name="BrowserTabItem">
                <Grid Background="{DynamicResource BgDark}">
                    <Grid.RowDefinitions>
                        <RowDefinition Height="Auto"/>
                        <RowDefinition Height="Auto"/>
                        <RowDefinition Height="*"/>
                    </Grid.RowDefinitions>

                    <!-- Address bar -->
                    <Grid Grid.Row="0" Margin="8,8,8,4">
                        <Grid.ColumnDefinitions>
                            <ColumnDefinition Width="Auto"/>
                            <ColumnDefinition Width="Auto"/>
                            <ColumnDefinition Width="Auto"/>
                            <ColumnDefinition Width="*"/>
                        </Grid.ColumnDefinitions>
                        <Button Grid.Column="0" Content="◀" Click="Back_Click" ToolTip="Back"/>
                        <Button Grid.Column="1" Content="▶" Click="Forward_Click" ToolTip="Forward"/>
                        <Button Grid.Column="2" Content="⌂" Click="Home_Click" ToolTip="Workshop Home"/>
                        <TextBox x:Name="AddressBar" Grid.Column="3" Margin="6,0,0,0"
                                 VerticalContentAlignment="Center" KeyDown="AddressBar_KeyDown"/>
                    </Grid>

                    <!-- Action buttons -->
                    <StackPanel Grid.Row="1" Orientation="Horizontal" Margin="8,0,8,6">
                        <TextBlock Text="Folder:" Foreground="{DynamicResource FgText}" VerticalAlignment="Center" Margin="3"/>
                        <TextBlock x:Name="DestFolderLabel" Text="Not set" Foreground="{DynamicResource AccentBlue}"
                                   VerticalAlignment="Center" Margin="0,0,10,0" MaxWidth="260"
                                   TextTrimming="CharacterEllipsis"/>

1. **Main Application**: WPF desktop app (Windows only, .NET 8)
2. **Core Functionality**: Downloads and manages Project Zomboid mods from Steam Workshop
3. **Key Components**:
   - MainWindow: Main hub with tabs and UI logic (~1470 lines)
   - SteamCmdService: Handles SteamCMD bootstrap and downloads
   - WorkshopApiService: Minimal API wrapper for Steam details
   - WorkshopVisualService: Fetches preview images and tags
   - WorkshopPageService: Fetches dependency information from Steam pages
   - Services for persistence: SettingsService, DownloadHistoryStore, UninstalledModsStore, ThumbnailStore

4. **Tabs**:
   - Browser: Embedded WebView2 to browse Steam Workshop
   - Downloaded Mods: Lists installed mods, shows version info, dependencies
   - Uninstalled Mods: Lists mods you've removed (from UninstalledModsStore)
   - Updater: Check for updates and download/force redownload

5. **Features**:
   - Batch download queue
   - Mod dependency resolution (require= fields from mod.info)
   - Dependency popup with "Show Deps" button
   - Visual features: thumbnails, tag filtering, tile/list views
   - Settings: themes, fonts, auto-refresh, backup
   - Mod import/export
   - Version tracking using ContentManifestId

6. **Dependency Handling**:
   - Require fields: numeric workshop IDs or backslash-prefixed internal names
   - Resolution via NormalizeModIdentifier and identifier index
   - Two-tier: numeric deps auto-queue, name-only deps open Steam search

7. **Visual System (Batch 4)**:
   - Tag filter sidebar with checkboxes
   - Shared collections between grid and tiles
   - Thumbnail downloads with throttling (SemaphoreSlim)
   - Dynamic theme switching

The application is a Project Zomboid Workshop Downloader that:
- Downloads mods from Steam Workshop
- Manages installed mods with version tracking
- Handles dependencies
- Provides a modern UI with multiple tabs
- Has visual features like thumbnails and tag filtering

- Manages uninstalled mods
- Supports batch updates
- Has various settings for customization

Let me provide a comprehensive organized explanation.

## Project Zomboid Workshop Downloader - Application Analysis

### What the application does

**Project Zomboid Workshop Downloader** is a modern desktop application for managing Project Zomboid mods from Steam Workshop. It automates downloading, updating, and managing mods while providing a visually rich interface with full workshop integration.

**Core functions:**
- Download mods directly from Steam Workshop using SteamCMD (embedded, ~5MB bootstrap)
- Scan and list installed mods, detect updates via Steam API manifest IDs
- Resolve and manage mod dependencies (both numeric IDs and internal names)
- Queue and batch download multiple mods simultaneously
- View/download mod thumbnails and Steam tags
- Filter installed mods by tags
- Export/import mod lists as XML
- Backup mods before updates
- Track download history
- Manage uninstalled mods for easy reinstallation

### How it works

**1. Download Flow (Downloader Tab)**
- User navigates to Steam Workshop pages (embedded WebView2)
- Click "Download Current" or "Add to Queue" from the browser page
- Downloads are serialized via SteamCMD with a single-process lock (`RunLock`) to ensure stability
- After download, Steam API checks manifest ID (`hcontent_file`) and records version
- Files are installed in `modsFolder/<workshopId> <modFolderName>/` format
- If mod info has a `name=` field, that's used as the folder name instead of raw subfolder names

**2. Installed Mods Scan (Updater/Installed Mods Tab)**
- Scans `modsFolder` for directories matching numeric workshop IDs or `mod.info` files
- Builds two indexes:
  - `installedWorkshopIds` - real numeric IDs (folder prefixes)
  - `identifierIndex` - maps `require=` names/IDs to workshop IDs
- Makes single Steam API call per mod to get current metadata
- Compares `LocalModVersions` manifest ID against live Steam manifest ID to detect updates
- Resolves each mod's `require=` entries against the `identifierIndex`
- Missing deps are marked; missing numeric deps can be queued; missing name-only deps trigger Steam search

**3. Dependency Resolution (Batch 3)**
- **Requirement sources:**
  - `mod.info` `require=` entries (either numeric workshop ID or internal names like `\NeatUI_Framework`)
  - Steam Workshop page HTML "Required items" section (only on explicit "Show Deps" click)
- **Resolution is purely local:**
  - `NormalizeModIdentifier("NeatUI Framework")` → "neatui framework" (case-normalized)
  - Checks both `identifierIndex` (name matches) and `installedWorkshopIds` (exact ID)
  - No extra Steam API calls for existing mods

**4. Visual System (Batch 4)**
- **Batched API requests** for preview/thumbnail URLs and tags (100 items per call)
- **Thumbnails** downloaded via `ThumbnailGate` semaphore (max 4 concurrent) to avoid CDN hammering
- **Tile view** mirrors same collection as grid view; tag filter applies to both
- **Tag sidebar** built from union of all installed mods' Steam tags
- **Update pulse animation:** Opacity pulse (1.0→0.45) via `DoubleAnimation` when `NeedsUpdate` is true
- **Thumbnail placeholders:** First letter of mod name as fallback until image arrives

**5. Queue System**
- `QueueList` items are window-level (visible on any tab when non-empty)
- Queue items persist until cleared or processed
- `StartQueue_Click` runs through all queued mods sequentially
- Status updates streamed from SteamCMD output via Dispatcher (UI thread safety)

**6. Update Flow**
- "Update All" removes old folder, downloads new, re-scans
- "RemoveOldModFolder" deletes the current folder before download to handle name mismatches
- Backups stored in `modsFolder/_backups/<modName>/<timestamp>/`
- Manifest ID comparison ensures accurate version tracking

**7. Uninstalled Mods**
- When you click "Uninstall", folder deleted and entry saved to `uninstalled_mods.json`
- Reinstall downloads from workshop and removes entry from list
- "Forget" removes entry from history but leaves folder

**8. Mod Identification (Critical)**
- **True workshop ID = numeric folder prefix** and workshop URL `?id=N`
- `mod.info` `id=` field is **NOT** usable for identification—only for `require=` resolution
- `TryExtractWorkshopId()` tries folder prefix first, then scans `mod.info` for numeric `id=`

**9. UI/UX Features**
- **4 themes:** Light, Dark, Midnight, Forest, Nord, Dracula, Solarized Dark/Light, Gruvbox, Monokai
- **Theme application:** DynamicResource brushes (`BgDark`, `BgPanel`, `BgField`, `FgText`, `AccentBlue`, `AccentGreen`, `BorderCol`) replaced entirely via `SetBrush` (WPF freezes XAML-declared brushes)
- **Font sizes:** App-level DynamicResources (`UIFontSizeGeneral/Button/Tab/Log`) updated via sliders
- **Log panel:** Dispatcher-safe, max 500 entries, auto-scroll only if already at bottom, "Jump to Bottom" button for others
- **Batch 4 view toggles:** Installed/Downloads/Uninstalled all support List vs Tile views, shared thumbnail data

### Project Structure

**Main components:**

1. **MainWindow.xaml(.cs)** (~1470 lines) - Hub for all functionality:
   - All tabs (Browser, Installed Mods, Updates), queue, download flow, scan/update logic, settings, theming
   - Observable collections: `_queue`, `_downloadedMods`, `_downloads`, `_uninstalledMods`
   - Session caches: `_depsPageCache` for Workshop page lookups, `_depsFetchInFlight` prevents duplicate clicks
   - Visual subsystem: `_selectedTags`, `TagFilterPanel`, `InstalledTiles/DownloadsTiles/UninstalledTiles`, `ModTileSize` slider

2. **Services/SteamCmdService.cs** (294 lines) - SteamCMD bootstrap + downloads:
   - `EnsureSteamCmdAsync()` - Downloads `steamcmd.zip` (~5MB) to `LocalData\PZWorkshopDownloader\steamcmd\` on first run
   - `DownloadModAsync()` - Executes `+workshop_download_item` command, installs to `modsFolder/<id> <name>/`, returns all installed folders
   - `GetRequiresFields()` - Parses `require=` entries from `mod.info`, removes `\` prefixes and commas/semicolons
   - `GetModIdentifiers()` - Returns `id=` and `name=` for `require=` resolution; returns empty for mods without `mod.info`

3. **Services/WorkshopApiService.cs** (95 lines) - Minimal API wrapper:
   - `GetDetailsAsync()` - Calls Steam `GetPublishedFileDetails` for metadata (title, file_size, time_created/updated, creator, `hcontent_file`)
   - Returns `WorkshopItemDetails` DTO with manifest ID for version comparison

4. **Services/WorkshopVisualService.cs** (86 lines) - Thumbs + tags:
   - Fetches `preview_url` and `tags` from same API in chunks of 100 IDs
   - Returns `WorkshopVisual` DTO with list of tags

5. **Services/WorkshopPageService.cs** (75 lines) - HTML scraping for "Show Deps":
   - Downloads mod page HTML, regexes "requiredItemsContainer" for `<a href="...?id=N">` links
   - Returns `WorkshopRequiredItem` list (id + title)

6. **Models/** - Plain DTOs (no INPC):
   - `ModRecord` (INPC for thumbnail/tags) - Installed mod details, deps, version, manifest ID
   - `DownloadTask` (INPC for thumbnail) - History item, progress, status
   - `QueueItem`, `UninstalledModEntry`, `DownloadHistoryEntry`, `LogEntry`

7. **Persistence:**
   - `settings.json` - Mods folder, themes, font sizes, `LocalModVersions`, `InstallDates`
   - `download_history.json` - DownloadTask entries
   - `uninstalled_mods.json` - UninstalledModEntry entries

8. **Data locations:**
   - All data under `%LOCALAPPDATA%\PZWorkshopDownloader\`
   - SteamCMD cache: `...\steamcmd\steamapps\workshop\content\108600\<id>\`
   - Installed mods: `modsFolder/<id> <name>/`

**Key patterns:**
- **Dispatcher safety** - SteamCMD output marshaled to UI for log/task detail updates
- **Manifest ID as version** - `hcontent_file` changes only when file content changes, unlike `time_updated`
- **Single-threaded** - Download queue serializes operations via `RunLock`
- **Batched API calls** - Visual fetches (100 items) minimize requests
- **Tag filtering** - Applied to both grid and tile views via `CollectionViewSource.GetDefaultView`

+        <member name="M:Microsoft.Web.WebView2.Core.CoreWebView2.AddHostObjectToScript(System.String,System.Object)">
+            <summary>
+            Adds the provided host object to script running in the WebView with the specified name.
+            </summary>
+            <param name="name">The name of the host object.</param>
+            <param name="rawObject">The host object to be added to script.</param>
+            <remarks>
+            Host objects are exposed as host object proxies via <c>window.chrome.webview.hostObjects.{name}</c>. Host object proxies are promises and will resolve to an object representing the host object. Only the COM visible objects/properties/methods can be accessed from script.
+            The app can control which part of .NET objects are exposed using <see cref="T:System.Runtime.InteropServices.ComVisibleAttribute"/>.
+            
+            JavaScript code in the WebView will be able to access appObject as following and then access attributes and methods of appObject.
+            
+            Note that while simple types, <c>IDispatch</c> and array are supported, and <c>IUnknown</c> objects that also implement <c>IDispatch</c> are treated as <c>IDispatch</c>, generic <c>IUnknown</c>, <c>VT_DECIMAL</c>, or <c>VT_RECORD</c> variant is not supported. Remote JavaScript objects like callback functions are represented as an <c>VT_DISPATCH</c> VARIANT with the object implementing <c>IDispatch</c>. The JavaScript callback method may be invoked using DISPID_VALUE for the DISPID. Such callback method invocations will return immediately and will not wait for the JavaScript function to run and so will not provide the return value of the JavaScript function. Nested arrays are supported up to a depth of 3. Arrays of by reference types are not supported. <c>VT_EMPTY</c> and <c>VT_NULL</c> are mapped into JavaScript as <c>null</c>. In JavaScript <c>null</c> and <c>undefined</c> are mapped to <c>VT_EMPTY</c>.
+            
+            Additionally, all host objects are exposed as <c>window.chrome.webview.hostObjects.sync.{name}</c>. Here the host objects are exposed as synchronous host object proxies. These are not promises and calls to functions or property access synchronously block running script waiting to communicate cross process for the host code to run. Accordingly this can result in reliability issues and it is recommended that you use the promise based asynchronous <c>window.chrome.webview.hostObjects.{name}</c> API described above.
+            
+            Synchronous host object proxies and asynchronous host object proxies can both proxy the same host object. Remote changes made by one proxy will be reflected in any other proxy of that same host object whether the other proxies and synchronous or asynchronous.
+            
+            While JavaScript is blocked on a synchronous call to native code, that native code is unable to call back to JavaScript. Attempts to do so will fail with <c>HRESULT_FROM_WIN32(ERROR_POSSIBLE_DEADLOCK)</c>.
+            
+            Host object proxies are JavaScript Proxy objects that intercept all property get, property set, and method invocations. Properties or methods that are a part of the Function or Object prototype are run locally. Additionally any property or method in the array <c>chrome.webview.hostObjects.options.forceLocalProperties</c> will also be run locally. This defaults to including optional methods that have meaning in JavaScript like <c>toJSON</c> and <c>Symbol.toPrimitive</c>. You can add more to this array as required.
+            
+            There's a method <c>chrome.webview.hostObjects.cleanupSome</c> that will best effort garbage collect host object proxies.
+            
+            The <c>chrome.webview.hostObjects.options</c> object provides the ability to change some functionality of host objects.
+            
+            <list type="table">
+            <listheader>
+            <term>Options property</term>
+            <description>Details</description>
+            </listheader>
+            <item>
+            <term><c>forceLocalProperties</c></term>
+            <description>
+            This is an array of host object property names that will be run locally, instead of being called on the native host object. This defaults to <c>then</c>, <c>toJSON</c>, <c>Symbol.toString</c>, and <c>Symbol.toPrimitive</c>. You can add other properties to specify that they should be run locally on the JavaScript host object proxy.
+            </description>
+            </item>
+            <item>
+            <term><c>log</c></term>
+            <description>
+            This is a callback that will be called with debug information. For example, you can set this to <c>console.log.bind(console)</c> to have it print debug information to the console to help when troubleshooting host object usage. By default this is null.
+            </description>
+            </item>
+            <item>
+            <term><c>shouldSerializeDates</c></term>
+            <description>
+            By default this is false, and JavaScript Date objects will be sent to host objects as a string using <c>JSON.stringify</c>. You can set this property to true to have Date objects properly serialize as a <c>System.DateTime</c> when sending to the .NET host object, and have <c>System.DateTime</c> properties and return values create a JavaScript <c>Date</c> object.
+            </description>
+            </item>
+            <item>
+            <term><c>defaultSyncProxy</c></term>
+            <description>
+            When calling a method on a synchronous proxy, the result should also be a synchronous proxy. But in some cases, the sync/async context is lost (for example, when providing to native code a reference to a function, and then calling that function in native code). In these cases, the proxy will be asynchronous, unless this property is set.
+            </description>
+            </item>
+            <item>
+            <term><c>forceAsyncMethodMatches</c></term>
+            <description>
+            This is an array of regular expressions. When calling a method on a synchronous proxy, the method call will be performed asynchronously if the method name matches a string or regular expression in this array. Setting this value to <c>Async</c> will make any method that ends with Async be an asynchronous method call. If an async method doesn't match here and isn't forced to be asynchronous, the method will be invoked synchronously, blocking execution of the calling JavaScript and then returning the resolution of the promise, rather than returning a promise.
+            </description>
+            </item>
+            <item>
+            <term><c>ignoreMemberNotFoundError</c></term>
+            <description>
+            By default, an exception is thrown when attempting to get the value of a proxy property that doesn't exist on the corresponding native class. Setting this property to <c>true</c> switches the behavior to match Chakra WinRT projection (and general JavaScript) behavior of returning <c>undefined</c> with no error.
+            </description>
+            </item>
+            <item>
+            <term><c>shouldPassTypedArraysAsArrays</c></term>
+            <description>
+            By default, typed arrays are passed to the host as <c>IDispatch</c>. To instead pass typed arrays to the host as <c>array</c>, set this to <c>true</c>.
+            </description>
+            </item>
+            </list>
+            
+            Host object proxies additionally have the following methods:
+            
+            <list type="table">
+            <listheader>
+            <term>Method name</term>
+            <description>Details</description>
+            </listheader>
+            <item>
+            <term><c>applyHostFunction</c>, <c>getHostProperty</c>, <c>setHostProperty</c></term>
+            <description>
+            Perform a method invocation, property get, or property set on the host object. You can use these to explicitly force a method or property to run remotely if there is a conflicting local method or property. For instance, <c>proxy.toString()</c> will run the local <c>toString</c> method on the proxy object. But <c>proxy.applyHostFunction('toString')</c> runs <c>toString</c> on the host proxied object instead.
+            </description>
+            </item>
+            <item>
+            <term><c>getLocalProperty</c>, <c>setLocalProperty</c></term>
+            <description>
+            Perform property get, or property set locally. You can use these methods to force getting or setting a property on the host object proxy itself rather than on the host object it represents. For instance, <c>proxy.unknownProperty</c> will get the property named <c>unknownProperty</c> from the host proxied object. But <c>proxy.getLocalProperty('unknownProperty')</c> will get the value of the property <c>unknownProperty</c> on the proxy object itself.
+            </description>
+            </item>
+            <item>
+            <term><c>addEventListener</c></term>
+            <description>
+            This method only exists on proxies for .NET objects. Bind the JavaScript handler to the C# event, so that the JavaScript handler can be called through the C# event. For example, <c>chrome.webview.hostObjects.sample.addEventListener('TestEvent', () => { alert('Invoked from remote');});</c> bind an anonymous JavaScript function to a C# event called 'TestEvent'. When calling <c>TestEvent?.Invoke()</c> on C# side, the JavaScript function that was just bound will be called asynchronously. It allows adding more than one handler for an event, but if the handler is already in the list of event handler, it will not be added a second time. If the host object cannot find the event with the name passed in by the <c>addEventListener</c> function or it is no public or its return type is not void, an exception will be thrown. If the count and type of C# event's parameters do not match the count and type of JavaScript handler, invoke <c>addEventListener</c> will be successful but an exception will be passed to JavaScript when invoke the event on C# side. If the host object has defined <c>addEventListener</c> function, use the defined function rather than the additionally <c>addEventListener</c> function.
+            </description>
+            </item>
+            <item>
+            <term><c>removeEventListener</c></term>
+            <description>
+            This method only exists on proxies for .NET objects. Removes a handler previously bound with <c>addEventListener()</c>. If the handler does not exist in the list of event handler, nothing will happen. If the host object cannot find the event with the name passed in by the <c>removeEventListener</c> function or it is no public, an exception will be thrown. If the host object has defined <c>removeEventListener</c> function, use the defined function rather than the additionally <c>removeEventListener</c> function.
+            </description>
+            </item>
+            <item>
+            <term><c>sync</c></term>
+            <description>
+            Asynchronous host object proxies expose a sync method which returns a promise for a synchronous host object proxy for the same host object. For example, <c>chrome.webview.hostObjects.sample.methodCall()</c> returns an asynchronous host object proxy. You can use the <c>sync</c> method to obtain a synchronous host object proxy instead:
+            <c>const syncProxy = await chrome.webview.hostObjects.sample.methodCall().sync()</c>
+            </description>
+            </item>
+            <item>
+            <term><c>async</c></term>
+            <description>
+            Synchronous host object proxies expose an async method which blocks and returns an asynchronous host object proxy for the same host object. For example, <c>chrome.webview.hostObjects.sync.sample.methodCall()</c> returns a synchronous host object proxy. Calling the <c>async</c> method on this blocks and then returns an asynchronous host object proxy for the same host object: <c>const asyncProxy = chrome.webview.hostObjects.sync.sample.methodCall().async()</c>
+            </description>
+            </item>
+            <item>
+            <term><c>then</c></term>
+            <description>
+            Asynchronous host object proxies have a then method. This allows them to be awaitable. <c>then</c> will return a promise that resolves with a representation of the host object. If the proxy represents a JavaScript literal then a copy of that is returned locally. If the proxy represents a function then a non-awaitable proxy is returned. If the proxy represents a JavaScript object with a mix of literal properties and function properties, then the a copy of the object is returned with some properties as host object proxies.
+            </description>
+            </item>
+            <item>
+            <term><c>cancelPromise</c></term>
+            <description>
+            This method attempts to cancel the fulfillment of a promised value. If the promise hasn't already been fulfilled and cancelation is supported, the promise will get rejected. <c>cancelPromise</c> supports cancelation of IAsyncOperation and IAsyncAction methods. If the promise is successfully canceled, then calling await on the promise will throw. For example, <c>chrome.webview.hostObjects.cancelPromise(promise); await promise;</c> will throw with "Promise Canceled". Once a promise has been canceled, a subsequent cancel on the same promise will throw an exception as well.
+            </description>
+            </item>
+            </list>
+            
+            All other property and method invocations (other than the above Remote object proxy methods, <c>forceLocalProperties</c> list, and properties on Function and Object prototypes) are run remotely. Asynchronous host object proxies return a promise representing asynchronous completion of remotely invoking the method, or getting the property. The promise resolves after the remote operations complete and the promises resolve to the resulting value of the operation. Synchronous host object proxies work similarly but block JavaScript execution and wait for the remote operation to complete.
+            
+            Setting a property on an asynchronous host object proxy works slightly differently. The set returns immediately and the return value is the value that will be set. This is a requirement of the JavaScript Proxy object. If you need to asynchronously wait for the property set to complete, use the <c>setHostProperty</c> method which returns a promise as described above. Synchronous object property set property synchronously blocks until the property is set.
+            
+            Exposing host objects to script has security risk. Please follow [best practices](/microsoft-edge/webview2/concepts/security).
+            </remarks>
+            <example>
+            To create a [IDispatch](/windows/win32/api/oaidl/nn-oaidl-idispatch) implementing class in C# use the following attributes on each class you intend to expose.
+            <code>
+            // Bridge and BridgeAnotherClass are C# classes that implement IDispatch and works with AddHostObjectToScript.
+            [ClassInterface(ClassInterfaceType.AutoDual)]
+            [ComVisible(true)]
+            public class BridgeAnotherClass
+            {
+                // Sample property.
+                public string Prop { get; set; } = "Example";
+            }
+            
+            [ClassInterface(ClassInterfaceType.AutoDual)]
+            [ComVisible(true)]
+            public class Bridge
+            {
+                public string Func(string param)
+                {
+                    return "Example: " + param;
+                }
+            
+                public BridgeAnotherClass AnotherObject { get; set; } = new BridgeAnotherClass();
+            
+                // Sample indexed property.
+                [System.Runtime.CompilerServices.IndexerName("Items")]
+                public string this[int index]
+                {
+                    get { return m_dictionary[index]; }
+                    set { m_dictionary[index] = value; }
+                }
+                private Dictionary<int, string> m_dictionary = new Dictionary<int, string>();
+            }
+            </code>
+            Then add instances of those classes via <see cref="M:Microsoft.Web.WebView2.Core.CoreWebView2.AddHostObjectToScript(System.String,System.Object)"/>:
+            <code>
+            webView.CoreWebView2.AddHostObjectToScript("bridge", new Bridge());
+            </code>
+            And then in script you can call the methods, and access those properties of the objects added via <see cref="M:Microsoft.Web.WebView2.Core.CoreWebView2.AddHostObjectToScript(System.String,System.Object)"/>.
+            Note that `CoreWebView2.AddHostObjectToScript` only applies to the top-level document and not to frames. To add host objects to frames use `CoreWebView2Frame.AddHostObjectToScript`.
+            <code>
+            // Find added objects on the hostObjects property
+            const bridge = chrome.webview.hostObjects.bridge;
+            
+            // Call a method and pass in a parameter.
+            // The result is another proxy promise so you must await to get the result.
+            console.log(await bridge.Func("testing..."));
+            
+            // A property may be another object as long as its class also implements
+            // IDispatch.
+            // Getting a property also gets a proxy promise you must await.
+            const propValue = await bridge.AnotherObject.Prop;
+            console.log(propValue);
+            
+            // Indexed properties
+            let index = 123;
+            bridge[index] = "test";
+            let result = await bridge[index];
+            console.log(result);
+            </code>
+            </example>
+            <seealso cref="T:System.Runtime.InteropServices.ComVisibleAttribute"/>
+        </member>

+        <member name="M:Microsoft.Web.WebView2.Core.CoreWebView2.AddWebResourceRequestedFilter(System.String,Microsoft.Web.WebView2.Core.CoreWebView2WebResourceContext)">
+            <summary>
+            Adds a URI and resource context filter for the <see cref="E:Microsoft.Web.WebView2.Core.CoreWebView2.WebResourceRequested"/> event.
+            </summary>
+            <param name="uri">An URI to be added to the <see cref="E:Microsoft.Web.WebView2.Core.CoreWebView2.WebResourceRequested"/> event.</param>
+            <param name="ResourceContext">A resource context filter to be added to the <see cref="E:Microsoft.Web.WebView2.Core.CoreWebView2.WebResourceRequested"/> event.</param>
+            <remarks>
+            A web resource request with a resource context that matches this filter's resource context and a URI that matches this filter's URI wildcard string will be raised via the <see cref="E:Microsoft.Web.WebView2.Core.CoreWebView2.WebResourceRequested"/> event.
+            
+            The <c>uri</c> parameter value is a wildcard string matched against the URI of the web resource request. This is a glob style wildcard string in which a <c>*</c> matches zero or more characters and a <c>?</c> matches exactly one character.
+            These wildcard characters can be escaped using a backslash just before the wildcard character in order to represent the literal <c>*</c> or <c>?</c>.
+            
+            The matching occurs over the URI as a whole string and not limiting wildcard matches to particular parts of the URI.
+            The wildcard filter is compared to the URI after the URI has been normalized, any URI fragment has been removed, and non-ASCII hostnames have been converted to punycode.
+            
+            Specifying a <c>nullptr</c> for the uri is equivalent to an empty string which matches no URIs.
+            
+            For more information about resource context filters, navigate to <see cref="T:Microsoft.Web.WebView2.Core.CoreWebView2WebResourceContext"/>.
+            
+            <list type="table">
+            <listheader>
+            <description>URI Filter String</description>
+            <description>Request URI</description>
+            <description>Match</description>
+            <description>Notes</description>
+            </listheader>
+            <item>
+            <description><c>*</c></description>
+            <description><c>https://contoso.com/a/b/c</c></description>
+            <description>Yes</description>
+            <description>A single * will match all URIs</description>
+            </item>
+            <item>
+            <description><c>*://contoso.com/*</c></description>
+            <description><c>https://contoso.com/a/b/c</c></description>
+            <description>Yes</description>
+            <description>Matches everything in contoso.com across all schemes</description>
+            </item>
+            <item>
+            <description><c>*://contoso.com/*</c></description>
+            <description><c>https://example.com/?https://contoso.com/</c></description>
+            <description>Yes</description>
+            <description>But also matches a URI with just the same text anywhere in the URI</description>
+            </item>
+            <item>
+            <description><c>example</c></description>
+            <description><c>https://contoso.com/example</c></description>
+            <description>No</description>
+            <description>The filter does not perform partial matches</description>
+            </item>
+            <item>
+            <description><c>*example</c></description>
+            <description><c>https://contoso.com/example</c></description>
+            <description>Yes</description>
+            <description>The filter matches across URI parts </description>
+            </item>
+            <item>
+            <description><c>*example</c></description>
+            <description><c>https://contoso.com/path/?example</c></description>
+            <description>Yes</description>
+            <description>The filter matches across URI parts</description>
+            </item>
+            <item>
+            <description><c>*example</c></description>
+            <description><c>https://contoso.com/path/?query#example</c></description>
+            <description>No</description>
+            <description>The filter is matched against the URI with no fragment</description>
+            </item>
+            <item>
+            <description><c>*example</c></description>
+            <description><c>https://example</c></description>
+            <description>No</description>
+            <description>The URI is normalized before filter matching so the actual URI used for comparison is <c>https://example.com/</c></description>
+            </item>
+            <item>
+            <description><c>*example/</c></description>
+            <description><c>https://example</c></description>
+            <description>Yes</description>
+            <description>Just like above, but this time the filter ends with a / just like the normalized URI</description>
+            </item>
+            <item>
+            <description><c>https://xn--qei.example/</c></description>
+            <description><c>https://❤.example/</c></description>
+            <description>Yes</description>
+            <description>Non-ASCII hostnames are normalized to punycode before wildcard comparison</description>
+            </item>
+            <item>
+            <description><c>https://❤.example/</c></description>
+            <description><c>https://xn--qei.example/</c></description>
+            <description>No</description>
+            <description>Non-ASCII hostnames are normalized to punycode before wildcard comparison</description>
+            </item>
+            </list>
+            </remarks>
+            <seealso cref="M:Microsoft.Web.WebView2.Core.CoreWebView2.RemoveWebResourceRequestedFilter(System.String,Microsoft.Web.WebView2.Core.CoreWebView2WebResourceContext)"/>
+            <seealso cref="T:Microsoft.Web.WebView2.Core.CoreWebView2WebResourceContext"/>
+            <seealso cref="E:Microsoft.Web.WebView2.Core.CoreWebView2.WebResourceRequested"/>
+        </member>

+        <member name="M:Microsoft.Web.WebView2.Core.CoreWebView2.TrySuspendAsync">
+            <summary>
+            An app may call this API to have the WebView2 consume less memory.
+            </summary>
+            <remarks>
+            This is useful when a Win32 app becomes invisible, or when a Universal Windows Platform app is being suspended, during the suspended event handler before completing the suspended event.
+            
+            The <see cref="P:Microsoft.Web.WebView2.Core.CoreWebView2Controller.IsVisible"/> property must be false when the API is called. Otherwise, the API throws COMException with error code of <c>HRESULT_FROM_WIN32(ERROR_INVALID_STATE)</c>.
+            
+            Suspending is similar to putting a tab to sleep in the Edge browser. Suspending pauses WebView script timers and animations, minimizes CPU usage for the associated browser renderer process and allows the operating system to reuse the memory that was used by the renderer process for other processes.
+            
+            Note that Suspend is best effort and considered completed successfully once the request is sent to browser renderer process. If there is a running script, the script will continue to run and the renderer process will be suspended after that script is done.
+            
+            See [Sleeping Tabs FAQ](https://techcommunity.microsoft.com/t5/articles/sleeping-tabs-faq/m-p/1705434) for conditions that might prevent WebView from being suspended. In those situations, the result of the async task is false.
+            
+            The WebView will be automatically resumed when it becomes visible. Therefore, the app normally does not have to call <see cref="M:Microsoft.Web.WebView2.Core.CoreWebView2.Resume"/> explicitly.
+            
+            The app can call <see cref="M:Microsoft.Web.WebView2.Core.CoreWebView2.Resume"/> and then <see cref="M:Microsoft.Web.WebView2.Core.CoreWebView2.TrySuspendAsync"/> periodically for an invisible WebView so that the invisible WebView can sync up with latest data and the page ready to show fresh content when it becomes visible.
+            
+            All WebView APIs can still be accessed when a WebView is suspended. Some APIs like Navigate will auto resume the WebView. To avoid unexpected auto resume, check <see cref="P:Microsoft.Web.WebView2.Core.CoreWebView2.IsSuspended"/> property before calling APIs that might change WebView state.
+            </remarks>

+            :::code language="csharp" source="../code/sample/SampleApps/WebView2WpfBrowser/MainWindow.xaml.cs" id="TrySuspend":::
+            </example>

+        <member name="M:Microsoft.Web.WebView2.Core.CoreWebView2.SetVirtualHostNameToFolderMapping(System.String,System.String,Microsoft.Web.WebView2.Core.CoreWebView2HostResourceAccessKind)">
+            <summary>
+            Sets a mapping between a virtual host name and a folder path to make available to web sites via that host name.
+            </summary>
+            <param name="hostName">A virtual host name.</param>
+            <param name="folderPath">A folder path name to be mapped to the virtual host name. The length must not exceed the Windows MAX_PATH limit.</param>
+            <param name="accessKind">The level of access to resources under the virtual host from other sites.</param>
+            <remarks>
+            <para>
+            After setting the mapping, documents loaded in the WebView can use HTTP or HTTPS URLs at the specified host name specified by <c>hostName</c> to access files in the local folder specified by <c>folderPath</c>.
+            This mapping applies to both top-level document and iframe navigations as well as subresource references from a document. This also applies to dedicated and shared worker scripts but does not apply to service worker scripts.
+            
+            Due to a current implementation limitation, media files accessed using virtual host name can be very slow to load.
+            
+            As the resource loaders for the current page might have already been created and running, changes to the mapping might not be applied to the current page and a reload of the page is needed to apply the new mapping.
+            
+            Both absolute and relative paths are supported for <c>folderPath</c>. Relative paths are interpreted as relative to the folder where the exe of the app is in.
+            </para>
+            <para>
+            For example, after calling <c>SetVirtualHostNameToFolderMapping("appassets.example", "assets", CoreWebView2HostResourceAccessKind.Deny);</c>, navigating to <c>https://appassets.example/my-local-file.html</c> will show content from my-local-file.html in the assets subfolder located on disk under the same path as the app's executable file.
+            
+            DOM elements that want to reference local files will have their host reference virtual host in the source. If there are multiple folders being used, define one unique virtual host per folder.
+            </para>
+            <para>
+            You should typically choose virtual host names that are never used by real sites.
+            If you own a domain such as <c>example.com</c>, another option is to use a subdomain reserved for the app (like <c>my-app.example.com</c>).
+            </para>
+            <para>
+            [RFC 6761](https://tools.ietf.org/html/rfc6761) has reserved several special-use domain names that are guaranteed to not be used by real sites (for example, <c>.example</c>, <c>.test</c>, and <c>.invalid</c>).
+            </para>
+            <para>
+            Note that using <c>.local</c> as the top-level domain name will work but can cause a delay during navigations. You should avoid using <c>.local</c> if you can.
+            </para>
+            <para>
+            Apps should use distinct domain names when mapping folder from different sources that should be isolated from each other. For instance, the app might use app-file.example for files that ship as part of the app, and book1.example might be used for files containing books from a less trusted source that were previously downloaded and saved to the disk by the app.
+            </para>
+            <para>
+            The host name used in the APIs is canonicalized using Chromium's host name parsing logic before being used internally.
+            For more information see [HTML5 2.6 URLs](https://dev.w3.org/html5/spec-LC/urls.html).
+            </para>
+            <para>
+            All host names that are canonicalized to the same string are considered identical.
+            For example, <c>EXAMPLE.COM</c> and <c>example.com</c> are treated as the same host name.
+            An international host name and its Punycode-encoded host name are considered the same host name. There is no DNS resolution for host name and the trailing '.' is not normalized as part of canonicalization.
+            </para>
+            <para>
+            Therefore <c>example.com</c> and <c>example.com.</c> are treated as different host names. Similarly, <c>virtual-host-name</c> and <c>virtual-host-name.example.com</c> are treated as different host names even if the machine has a DNS suffix of <c>example.com</c>.
+            </para>
+            <para>
+            Specify the minimal cross-origin access necessary to run the app. If there is not a need to access local resources from other origins, use <see cref="F:Microsoft.Web.WebView2.Core.CoreWebView2HostResourceAccessKind.Deny"/>.
+            </para>
+            </remarks>
+            <example>
+            <code>
+            webView.CoreWebView2.SetVirtualHostNameToFolderMapping(
+                "appassets.example", "assets", CoreWebView2HostResourceAccessKind.DenyCors);
+            webView.Source = new Uri("https://appassets.example/index.html");
+            </code>
+            
+            This in an example on how to embed a local image. For more information see <see cref="M:Microsoft.Web.WebView2.Core.CoreWebView2.NavigateToString(System.String)"/>.

+            webView.CoreWebView2.SetVirtualHostNameToFolderMapping(
